items.note: Sardula (Vyala/Virala): animal shape made by art, varieties Simha-, Nara-, Gaja-virala; carved in relief on walls between piers; cites Samarangana LVII. (SAMAR cited via Kramrisch)
Lion/sardula appear as brackets in Candela temple mandapas of Central India; sardula and makara are parts of the Kirttimukha.
Lion shape at the Vedi corners; lions on temple base and on the sikhara Vedi supporting the amalaka.

reject_reason: interpretive discussion of sardula and rider groups and the Dilipa story; generic

items.note: Lion-and-man group carved in the round before the temple; man riding the sardula on walls and pillars is the Ksatriya, royal knight.
Meru type to be built by a Ksatriya patron; sardula identifies patron with his temple; on Candella temples sardula alternates with apsaras.
Surasundari and Sakti images on the temple walls; sardula (vyala) and Sakti images alternate on Khajuraho walls and capitals; cites Samaranganasutradhara LVII.645. (SAMAR cited via Kramrisch)
Saktis or Yoginis figured on temple walls in all directions as Celestial Beauties beside the gods.
Celestial Beauties belong to the avarana-devatas, repeated all round the walls (Kandariya, Devi Jagadamba).
Names and types of Sakti images: Apsara, Nataka, Yaksini, Dig Devi; Apsara as movement in the atmosphere, Yaksini in vegetation.
Dig Devis (Women of the Quarters) referred to in inscriptions; Candela inscription and Ittagi inscription of A.D. 1112 cited. (footnote)
Salabhanjika (woman and tree) often carved on capital brackets; Nataka forms a bracket of the mandapa ceiling.
